title: Fitted positive input weights gave no clear block prediction gain at penalty 10 in 169 selected MICrONS targets
abstract: We tested whether fitted nonnegative input weights predict omitted entries of a target cell's mean movie response in one MICrONS mouse. We used 169 targets with at least five measured anatomical inputs and a ridge penalty of 10. In five block folds, mean scaled error was 2.27770; matched input sets gave 2.25550. The matched-set gain was -0.02221, with a descriptive target bootstrap interval of -0.11342 to 0.06765. The training-mean error was 2.04157. Interleaved folds gave positive-model error 1.18900 and matched error 1.21884. We also tested signed weights, equal pooling and penalties 1 and 100. Sparse inputs, shared stimuli and cells, one mouse, coarse matching and trial-mean data limit the test. It does not measure causal transmission or transfer across animals. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction. External records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Mean scaled error for two response-entry fold rules in one mouse. Lower error is better. Dashed lines show the matched positive-model mean. Penalty is 10.
